authority: orientation-only; no mutation, effect, proof, completion or issue-close authority
currentness: Read one repository revision; record each selected path and provider blob identity. Reconsider changed selected sources/dependencies; unrelated blobs do not invalidate the reading. Source identity is not truth or runtime admission.
recovery: If kind/source identity is absent, incompatible or stale, or a selected ref is missing/malformed, keep only directly observed repository facts. Follow the exact owner ref in OWNERSHIP.toml; ask a runtime-capable maintainer to restore the generated profile or reconcile the source. Do not guess an operating decision.

entries.select: Read the repository bootstrap and only task-relevant scoped instruction files; their paths/routes and checks/protect/reconcile metadata retain source authority. Local instructions are not repository-visible.

Follow system_intent.sources/preferred_source to repository intent and assurance.decision_record_target to settled decisions; absent intent configuration uses SYSTEM_INTENT.md and README.md. Policy bytes describe requirements, not observed runtime capabilities.
Choose a relevant semantic route with agent judgment; follow only its declared procedure path or registry_sources. An absent optional registry is not an unavailable runtime.

Prefer a task-supplied owner ref; otherwise follow active.execplans.surface in the optional state file or enumerate only immediate *.plan.json names, excluding archive. Select the relevant owner by meaning. Read intent.outcome/non_goals, scope, proof/relationships, blockers, next_action and continuation from that record; recorded status is not fresh proof or local active selection.

Use notes metadata (routes_from, semantic_routes and task_relevance) to select relevant note paths; follow only those notes and their stated dependencies. Treat notes as advisory, even if historical metadata says canonical or decision. Stale/superseded/contradicted or changed dependencies require reconsideration.

Read relevant requirements, protocol/source refs and proof/claim limits. Follow exact evidence refs only when needed. An asserted check, receipt or accepted progress is repository-recorded evidence, not a new successful check or permission to approve/close.
